mission_goal: Frank v0.1 voll lauffähig auf Andreas Ubuntu developer system

zero_cost_evidence.claim: NVIDIA Developer Program members have free access to hosted NIM API endpoints for prototyping; individual endpoints may be rate limited.
zero_cost_evidence.counterhypothesis: A configured credential can belong to a different billing or production context; request execution must still stay on the documented integrate.api.nvidia.com developer endpoint and emit a receipt.

response_bounds.claim: A bounded read must request one sentinel byte beyond the accepted limit to distinguish an oversized response from a response that merely fills the limit.
response_bounds.counterhypothesis: Reading exactly the accepted limit is sufficient; falsified because HTTPResponse.read(amt) returns only up to amt bytes and therefore cannot prove end-of-body at that boundary.

text_message_roles.claim: The plain-text adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; tool/function messages require the separate typed tool-calling path.
text_message_roles.counterhypothesis: An arbitrary nonempty role can be delegated to provider-side validation; falsified for this adapter because it causes an avoidable authenticated network call before the provider can reject it.

invariants: Never serialize, log, commit, echo or display API secret values.
Never access Together, including discovery, probes, routing and fallback.
Never make a paid request unless the project owner separately authorizes a nonzero budget.
A configured key is capability evidence, not proof of quota or health.
Except for an officially documented free developer endpoint, a configured key requires explicit host-side zero-cost attestation before routing.
A provider credential may only be sent to that provider's canonical host; a global multi-provider host allowlist is forbidden.
Credential binding compares the full remote origin boundary, including the effective HTTPS port; hostname equality alone is insufficient.
Provider endpoint URLs containing userinfo are rejected before request construction or network access.
Authenticated provider requests must not follow HTTP redirects; redirects fail closed before credentials can cross an origin boundary.
The text-chat adapter validates a nonempty model plus object messages with nonempty string roles and string content before network access; typed multimodal requests require a separate adapter.
The text-chat adapter accepts only system, user and assistant roles; arbitrary and tool/function roles are rejected before routing, credential use or network access.
Execution receipt request IDs bind provider, endpoint host and serialized request digest and remain stable across retries; attempt IDs are unique per execution attempt.
Attempt IDs include a fresh high-entropy nonce so equal-time concurrent attempts cannot alias; raw nonces are never serialized.
A response reaches VERIFIED only when choices is a non-empty list whose first message is an object with string content; malformed JSON shapes fail closed with a receipt.
An HTTP status response, including 429 and 5xx, proves EXECUTED transport but never VERIFIED or DONE; connection and timeout failures without an HTTP response remain unexecuted.
Every received non-2xx status remains unverified even when the transport returns it as a regular response object instead of raising HTTPError.
Malformed bodies preserve the received HTTP status and classify as invalid_provider_response; connection or timeout failures without a response use null status and unreachable_provider.
Once response headers and status are received, body-read failures preserve that status and EXECUTED while classifying as incomplete_provider_response; they never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Provider responses larger than 2000000 bytes are detected with a one-byte sentinel read, classified as provider_response_too_large, and never reach VERIFIED or DONE.
Every real provider request must emit a redacted execution receipt.
Rate limits and provider faults trigger bounded cooldown and rerouting, never retry storms.
